summary.text: Dale Strong is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Alabama's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2022. A lifelong first responder in Monrovia, he served 26 years in Madison County government, first as a county commissioner and then as the commission's first Republican chairman. In the 119th Congress he serves on the Appropriations Committee, where he is Vice Chair of the Commerce, Justice, Science Subcommittee, and chairs a Homeland Security subcommittee.

paragraphs.text: Born in Monrovia, Alabama, and graduated from Sparkman High School (1988, per Wikipedia). He is the son of a founding member of the Monrovia Fire-Rescue Department.
Earned a B.S. in business administration from Athens State University, and an EMT license from the University of Alabama in Huntsville, according to Wikipedia.

According to his official biography, he has spent his adult life as a first responder: a junior volunteer firefighter and 911 dispatcher who has 35 years of service as an EMT and 41 years as a volunteer firefighter. Wikipedia adds earlier jobs in public relations at First Alabama Bank and as a sales representative for Solvay.

First elected to the Madison County Commission in 1996, according to Wikipedia, as the youngest elected Republican official in Alabama at the time; his official biography says he served in local government for 26 years.
Elected chairman of the Madison County Commission in 2012, the first Republican to hold the post; he served until resigning on January 2, 2023.

Won the 2022 Republican primary for the open seat of Rep. Mo Brooks, defeating Casey Wardynski in a June 21 runoff with about 63%, then won the general election with about 67% against Democrat Kathy Warner-Stanton, according to Wikipedia.

Sworn in January 2023. Serves on the House Appropriations Committee, with subcommittee roles as Vice Chair of Commerce, Justice, Science, plus Transportation, Housing and Urban Development and Legislative Branch, and chairs the Homeland Security Emergency Management and Technology Subcommittee.
According to his official biography, he is married to Laura Toney Strong and they have two children, Whitney and Harrison.
